newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees higher EU sugar output for 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees higher EU sugar output for 1996/97.

text.p: The European Union (EU should produce 17.40 million tonnes of sugar in raw value terms in 1996/97, 392,000 tonnes above the output figure for 1995/96, German statistician F.O. Licht said on Wednesday. In its second estimate of European beet sugar production for the current crop year, Licht said total European output would reach 29.35 million tonnes after a previous 28.54 million.
"A mild autumn in Western Europe and an absence of severe frosts in Eastern Europe have improved the continent's sugar production prospects," Licht said.
Licht said France would produce 4.57 million tonnes of beet sugar in 1996/97, after the EU's key producer turned out 4.60 million in 1995/96.
Sugar output in Germany, the trading bloc's second largest producer, was estimated at 4.42 million tonnes after a previous 4.16 million, it said.
In its first estimate of European 1996/97 beet sugar production, Licht pegged EU output at 16.47 million tonnes and total European output at 27.83 million.
In western Europe's three non-EU nations -- Turkey, the former Yugoslavia and Switzerland -- production was also expected to be considerably higher, it said.
Turkish production was estimated at 2.01 million tonnes compared with 1.38 million in 1995/96, while the former Yugoslavia would turn out 452,000 tonnes after 307,000.
Switzerland was expected to produce 207,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996/97, Licht said. It produced 140,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
